name: PlanComparison
description: Mortar marketing plan comparison, using central semantic tokens.

props.title: string
props.featuredTone: "muted" | "accent" (default "muted"; accent tints the featured column with the brand's selected colour and puts its header in the link colour)
props.groups: { label?; rows: { feature; values: ComparisonValue[] }[] }[] (a group without a label renders no group header row)
props.align: "start" | "center" (default "center"; start aligns sentence-length values to the start edge and the top of the row)
props.layout: "section" | "flush" (default "section"; flush drops the section padding, rule and width cap so the table lines up with the surrounding content)
props.id: string (the root element's id, e.g. an in-page link target)
props.className: string (layout only: margins or grid placement)

contract.usage: Import { PlanComparison } from @tonycodes-ui/mortar. Compose with the public typed props. A value is a string, a boolean (a ✓ or — mark) or { included, text } (a ✓ or ✗ mark before the text). For a long-form "us vs them" comparison with sentence-length values, use align="start", featuredTone="accent", { included, text } values and an unlabelled group; use layout="flush" inside a page column that already sets its own width and padding.
contract.avoid: Do not copy implementations, override central colours or grant component approval.
contract.accessibility: Verify accessible names, keyboard interaction, visible focus, responsive layout and supported states. The root element exposes data-m-component for tests and consumers. It is not a styling hook. The table is named by the section title, and on narrow screens it scrolls inside a focusable region named "<title> table". Included and not-included cells hide their glyph and carry screen-reader text ("Included" / "Not included", followed by the text for { included, text } values). The accent featured column keeps ink, secondary and link text at 4.5:1 in light and dark.
